key_insight: Ataraxis Breast CTX predicted disease-free survival in node-positive, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, while evidence for predicting chemotherapy benefit remained exploratory.
clinical_relevance: This AI biomarker could offer a tissue-sparing approach to risk assessment in postmenopausal patients, but its role in chemotherapy selection requires further validation.
method: Analyzed digitized H&E slides from 677 SWOG-8814 trial participants.
Compared histology-only and multimodal scores incorporating clinical variables.
Used locked model weights and thresholds, with predictions blinded to outcomes and no trial-data retraining.
evidence_signal: The multimodal score was associated with disease-free survival (HR 1.60, 95% CI 1.44–1.78; C-index 0.66), but the exploratory chemotherapy interaction was not statistically significant (p = 0.053).
watch_item: Only 46% of trial participants were analyzed, and chemotherapy-benefit prediction needs prospective validation before clinical use.
paper_title: AI-based prognosis and chemotherapy benefit in node-positive, HR+ breast cancer: a blinded external validation on SWOG-8814 trial
